title: TanStack Query: Server State Caching, Mutations & AI Streaming
description: Master TanStack Query v5 for enterprise server state: stale-while-revalidate caching, optimistic mutations for conversation management, infinite scroll for history, and integrating the streaming chat hook with query invalidation.

data.text: Server State: The Category That RTK and Context Cannot Handle

Server state is fundamentally different from client state: it is remote, asynchronously fetched, potentially stale, and shared with multiple users who may mutate it concurrently. Managing server state in Redux requires manual request tracking, caching logic, invalidation, and background refetch strategies—thousands of lines of boilerplate. TanStack Query v5 treats server state as a reactive cache: fetch once, serve instantly from cache, refresh in background, and invalidate automatically on mutations.

data.caption: TanStack Query Stale-While-Revalidate Caching Lifecycle
data.code:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Loading : First useQuery call / Cache empty
    Loading --> Fresh : Successful fetch (staleTime not elapsed)
    Fresh --> Stale : staleTime window expires
    Stale --> Fetching : Component mounts / Window refocuses / Manual invalidate
    Fetching --> Fresh : Successful background refetch
    Fetching --> Error : Network failure
    Error --> Fetching : Retry (3 attempts with exponential back-off)
    Fresh --> Offline : Network disconnect
    Offline --> Fetching : Network reconnects

data.text: TanStack Query v5 uses object-based query options with `queryKey` for cache partitioning and automatic refetch triggering.

data.text: Optimistic Mutations for Instant UI Updates

When a user renames a conversation, waiting 500ms for the server round-trip before updating the sidebar feels sluggish. Optimistic mutations update the UI cache immediately, then roll back if the server rejects the change.

data.content: Updating the conversation list cache immediately while the PATCH request is in flight.

data.title: useInfiniteQuery for Paginated Message History
data.content: Loading older messages in a conversation as the user scrolls to the top of the chat window.

data.title: Invalidate After Streaming Completes
data.content: After an AI streaming response finishes, call `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['conversations', tenantId] })` to refresh the conversation list sidebar. This ensures the conversation's `updatedAt` timestamp and `messageCount` reflect the new message without a manual page refresh.

data.title: TanStack Query Implementation Checklist
items: QueryKey arrays always include all variables the queryFn depends on (tenantId, userId)
staleTime configured appropriately: 0 for real-time data, 2-5 minutes for relatively static lists
Mutations use onMutate for optimistic updates with rollback via onError context snapshots
onSettled always calls invalidateQueries to sync from server after any mutation
useInfiniteQuery used for paginated lists; getNextPageParam extracts cursor from response
enabled flag prevents queries from firing before auth token or required IDs are available

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: TanStack Query eliminates server state management boilerplate with stale-while-revalidate caching.
Optimistic mutations deliver instant UI feedback with automatic rollback on failures.
useInfiniteQuery handles paginated data with cursor-based pagination out of the box.
Next, we learn React Hook Form with Zod schema validation for type-safe form state management.
data.takeaway: Treat server state as a reactive cache, not as data to be stored in Redux: TanStack Query handles freshness, retries, background sync, and optimistic updates automatically.
